parameters.query:
-- Claim this email. A repeat returns no row, so the run stops before Claude.
-- Exception: if the earlier run failed (the error workflow set status 'failed'),
-- the repeat takes over the row and the email gets a fresh try.
INSERT INTO email_log (message_id, mailpit_id, from_address, subject, execution_id)
VALUES ($1, $2, $3, $4, $5)
ON CONFLICT (message_id) DO UPDATE
  SET status = 'received', execution_id = EXCLUDED.execution_id, updated_at = now()
  WHERE email_log.status = 'failed'
RETURNING message_id;

INSERT INTO ai_usage (message_id, model, input_tokens, output_tokens, cost_usd, route)
VALUES ($1, $2, $3, $4, $5, $6);

parameters.subject: =Approve booking? {{ $json.item }} ({{ $json.start_date }})

parameters.query:
-- One statement, so both writes happen or neither does:
-- insert the booking, then mark the email approved.
-- If this email already has a booking, nothing is inserted, nothing is updated,
-- no row comes back, and so no second confirmation is sent.
WITH new_booking AS (
  INSERT INTO bookings (message_id, request_type, item, start_date, end_date,
                        production, requester_name, requester_email, notes)
  VALUES ($1, $2, $3, $4::date, $5::date, $6, $7, $8, $9)
  ON CONFLICT (message_id) DO NOTHING
  RETURNING id
)
UPDATE email_log SET status = 'approved', updated_at = now()
WHERE message_id = $1 AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM new_booking)
RETURNING (SELECT id FROM new_booking) AS booking_id;

-- One statement, so both writes happen or neither does:
-- save the reply draft, then mark the email needs_info.
WITH draft AS (
  INSERT INTO reply_drafts (message_id, to_address, subject, body)
  VALUES ($1, $2, $3, $4)
)
UPDATE email_log SET status = 'needs_info', updated_at = now() WHERE message_id = $1;
UPDATE email_log SET status = 'ignored', updated_at = now() WHERE message_id = $1;
